view.lede: The Downs, right-handed: one of the five generic courses that every course without its own build races on for now (undulating, downhill turn), with the bigger of its two stand sides. A rolling triangle of about 1m4f on the downs: a climb along the back straight, a sweeping downhill turn into a 3f run-in that rises again in the last furlong, and a downhill 7f straight course. Dressed as a downland course.
notes: Brighton and Lingfield (turf), and the two big downland courses until their own builds are in the game.
About 12.5f round, a 2.89f run-in. Drawn from a few numbers (the corners and bends of the loop, the chutes), so it can be reshaped quickly.
Downland course: old small stands and pavilions clustered round the winning post, near the end of the straight, the crowd up to the rail, the festival in the infield opposite.
Choose Medium or Low under Quality in the race view's bar. Auto steps down by itself.
